pending_interview.category: Behavioral/leadership — conflict resolution, prioritization under ambiguity, influence without authority, giving hard feedback, scaling a team through change
pending_interview.question: You joined a company six months ago to lead an AI engineering team. You've identified that a senior engineer on the team — one who has been there for five years, is well-liked, and is seen as a technical authority — consistently resists adopting the new development practices you're trying to establish, and their resistance is visibly influencing other team members to slow-walk the changes. Your manager has told you the transformation is a top priority for the business. How do you handle it?
